note: Every source this pack is built from, with the size and SHA-256 measured on 2026-10-10.
`evidence.quote` is the exact sentence the licence was read from, on `evidence.url`; a source
without one is not used, and the builder refuses bytes that do not match `bytes` and `sha256`.
Two licence bases carry this pack. (1) Works of the U.S. Government are not subject to copyright
in the United States (17 U.S.C. 105(a), quoted verbatim on the govinfo page named below); the
Farmers' Bulletins and the Bureau of Agricultural Chemistry and Engineering circular are
federal publications, and each scan prints its own Department of Agriculture imprint, which
`docs/packs/make.md` records. (2) Project Gutenberg's own rights statement for these ebooks is
`Public domain in the USA.` (read from each ebook's `.opds`), and Gutenberg's licence page
states the reuse position quoted below. Wikibooks pages are CC BY-SA 4.0 and keep their own
labelled chapter in the pack, so the share-alike boundary is a folder rather than a memory.
`kind` chooses the converter: `gutenberg-html` is a Gutenberg HTML edition (text, headings,
tables and the edition's own captioned figures), `ia-ocr` is the Internet Archive's OCR text
layer of a scanned bulletin, and `wikibooks` is a MediaWiki page's wikitext.
`furniture` is what the OCR layer adds to a document rather than being part of it: the scanning
library's banner and stamps. Each pattern is a `/pattern/flags` expression matched against the
collapsed line, and a pattern that matches nothing stops the build rather than quietly
admitting the banner into the article.
`figuresSha256` is the digest over the figures a book ships: one line per file, `name space
SHA-256`, sorted by name, hashed as UTF-8 with a trailing newline. It pins a hundred drawings
in one field so the licence evidence above stays readable.
